title: "Comping rhythm: Strum: down-up eighths"
subtitle: "For guitar, built up a step at a time"

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Strum: down-up eighths**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

Every eighth note, down on the beat and up off it, leaning on 2 and 4.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Acoustic strum* and *Emo / pop-punk*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: down-up eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumEights"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Strum: downstrokes on the beat

Start with something simpler. One ringing downstroke on every beat. The first strum to learn, and the usual one for a slow song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-strum-quarters.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U

Down on 1 and 3, down-up on 2 and 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-strum-folk.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumFolk"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Strum: down-up eighths, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Every eighth note: down on the beat, up on the and. Lean on 2 and 4 to go with the snare. Keep the up-strokes lighter and on the top strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: down-up eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumEights"}},{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumFolk"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: down-up eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumEights"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: down-up eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumEights"}}]'></div>

## In other styles

## How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Strum: downstrokes on the beat](chords-strum-quarters.qmd), [Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U](chords-strum-folk.qmd).
- **Leads to:** [Strum: muted eighths, open in the chorus](chords-strum-punk.qmd), [Strum: sixteenths](chords-strum16.qmd): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Root eighths](bass-eighths.qmd) (bass line), [Driving eighths](chords-eighths.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Hi-hat: eighth notes](drums-hheighths.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in straight-eighth rock:** [Root eighths](bass-eighths.qmd) (bass line), [Rock backbeat](drums-rock.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah](chords-oompah.qmd), [Waltz in one](chords-waltz.qmd), [Ballad: rocking](chords-ball-rock.qmd), [Ballad: half-broken](chords-ball-broken.qmd), [Ballad: syncopated](chords-ball-sync.qmd), [Quarter-note chords](chords-quarters.qmd), [Triplet chords (12/8)](chords-triplets.qmd), [Driving eighths](chords-eighths.qmd).
